reception: External reception settled in the short-vector compilation community, for which alignment was a shared obstacle. Eichenberger, Wu, and O'Brien's vectorization for SIMD architectures with alignment constraints engages the paper in detail, the CELL processor compiler cites it as evidence, and work on runtime alignment and length conversion, on multi-platform auto-vectorization, and on SIMD compilation for embedded processors positions its own alignment handling relative to it. The idea traveled outside compilers as well: T4 adopted the congruence idea in compiling sequential code for speculative parallelization in hardware. The citations are not numerous and many are brief, but the detailed engagements come from groups whose own work centered on alignment analysis.
